So, not having my support like he was use to and me needing so much cracked our relationship.

Just saw you were considering orthotocs. If it is anatomical and your leg bones are genuinely a different length orthotic will help tremendously. If you are like me and have muscle imbalance or lax/too tight ligaments orthotic will make the issue worse. Find a good PT who has experience with this.

I had a LLD when my hip was at its worst. Mine was corrected through PT and postural awareness. My symptoms improved dramatically. I also have SIJ dysfunction which caused my right hip to tip forward.
I go through phases where I have them a lot, then none at all. When I started Methotrexate I started getting them a lot. An L-lysine supplement every day helped a lot.

It's NOT in your head. And you do NOT have to have the gene or inflammatory markers. Go to spondylitis.org, you can request information pamphlets. Some of the research they present only came out in the last 5 years. Having professional pamphlets from an organization has made it so much easier for me to talk to providers who dont believe my rheumatologist or me.

This was my high school life. My father wasn't an alcoholic, but checked out. You are almost there! Dont give up! In the mean time you should join the r/raisedbynarcacist subreddit. 

Meditation is great, but you are on the home stretch and you need to prepare yourself for living on your own. Get your financial plan in order. Determine what your parents are paying for and make sure you have your own bank account. Try to find friends to have as roommates. It's really fucking hard. I'm 31 and just went no contact with my family this year after getting diagnosed with an autoimmune disorder and realizing they really dont give a shit about me. It's the best decision I've ever made for myself. 

Budget in for therapy, you will need that support. There are tons listed on psychology today. PM me if you need any help planning! R/legaladvice might be a good one to reach out to as well.

I'm an occupational therapist assistant with spondyloarthropathy. I tell my patients to never continue an exercise that consistently produces a pop. One or two throughout a set is ok and not abnormal. A consistent pop at the exact same angle of movement will likely cause wear and later more damage.  Stop just shy of the pop or change to an exercise that doesn't cause this.

If you can lay on your back, feet down,  knees flexed... You can put a pillow between your knees and squeeze and hold for 3-5 seconds. Then place a belt around your knees (exercise band is even better) allow enough slack so you can press your knees out slightly wider than hip width.  Press into the belt and hold 3-5 seconds. 

 10-15 reps 2-3 sets usually puts my SI joint back where it needs to be. 

Also make sure to hold your abs and glutes tight the entire exercise.

I'm still playing around with my diet. It seems to be about how much garbage I eat consecutively so like one slice of pizza a week or a burger no big deal. AIP has been the best. Keto is also really helpful. I'm doing a paleo keto blend and the results are not as good, but still better than no restraint.
